brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 111089 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,493/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 111089) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,493/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout success is 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%, with about $13,493/min at risk and a 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-3]. Root blocker pid 111089 (adhoc_reporting) holds locks for 4.0s and blocks checkout sessions [DB-1]. No protected settlements are in flight [DB-2], and no active change-calendar window covers adhoc_reporting [BIZ-5]. However, adhoc_reporting is not in the workload registry, so owner, replayability, replay cost and interrupt policy are unknown [BIZ-2][BIZ-4]. Per I4, an unknown workload cannot be priced for termination, so the trade-off belongs to its owner. Waiting risks exceeding the 60s tolerance, but terminating an unknown workload without registry evidence cannot be accepted unilaterally.

audit.report: An unknown workload, adhoc_reporting (pid 111089), held a database lock while idle in transaction for 4.0 seconds, blocking checkout sessions. The Database Guardian proposed terminating it twice because checkout success fell from 53% to 27% over 30 seconds, risking about $13,493 per minute against a 95% SLO. The Continuity Guardian blocked both proposals because adhoc_reporting was not in the workload registry, had no owner, no priced interrupt cost, and no change-calendar evidence, violating invariants I2 and I4. No protected settlements were in flight. The negotiation escalated to on-call after 47 seconds and 2 rounds without executing any action, so the business is not yet recovered.
audit.root_cause: pid 111089 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction) held a lock for 4.0 seconds and blocked checkout sessions, degrading success to 27% over 30 seconds.
lessons: Register adhoc_reporting in the workload registry with an owner and interrupt cost so the next checkout lock blocker can be terminated without escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeated the same termination proposal in R2 after the Continuity Guardian cited missing registry and change-calendar evidence, wasting a round instead of probing those invariants first. The Continuity Guardian correctly identified invariant violations I2 and I4 but did not propose an alternative unblock action within the 60-second degradation tolerance.
follow_ups: Identify the owner of adhoc_reporting and add it to the workload registry with a priced interrupt cost.
Review change-calendar coverage for adhoc_reporting and document a pre-approved termination path for unregistered root blockers during checkout SLO breaches.
